items.title: 68427_Harry Edison oral history interview
items.q: he had Tab Smith in the band

ctx.x: You know, I never saw the connection.

Oh, we worked together around St. Louis a long time, Jo Jones and I. And Walter Page. And then a trumpet player, a tenor player, they added another tenor player to the band which is Gene Porter. He used to play with Earl Hines and then they had a band there who I just read in this book that they connected me with, Eddie Johnson and his Cracker Jacks. Harold Baker was playing with that band, see, and I never did play with the band. But I knew him quite well because they used to come through Columbus, Ohio. That's…

items.title: Harry Edison — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History
items.q: Naturally, they had a boy in there from St. Louis, Tab Smith, I knew him.

ctx.x: How did you fit in as a youngster, this was your first real name band, how did you fit in with Lucky’s band?
Naturally, they had a boy in there from St. Louis, Tab Smith, I knew him. And I knew Harold Arnold who enticed me to go to New York on this fake ticket under somebody else’s

name. But I was still scared of Lucky, the way he would talk. He didn’t know anything about music, one note from the other, but he was a great director. He would hear something arranged one time, he would know where he wanted the dynamics put. As you followed him, it was a beautiful show.
